name: Vitreous enamelling
summary: A thin coat of glass that is fused to iron or steel at about 800 °C. It makes a hard, bright, washable surface that resists heat and rust.
how: Clean the metal and coat it with a ground layer of glass powder and water.
Fire the part at 760 to 840 °C until the glass melts into one skin.
Apply a top coat of 0.1 to 0.3 mm in white or a single colour and fire it again.
Leave the edges rolled: the enamel chips at a sharp edge and shows the dark metal.

origin.note: Factories coat sheet iron and cast iron with glass powder, and the process makes cheap, washable pots, signs and baths.

adoptions.via: Factories and workshops fit enamelled steel shades, signs and fittings that are hard, bright and easy to wash.
